item.title: Democrats flip more seats in Congress as GOP grapples with stunning losses
item.description: After Democrats' sweeping House and Senate victories, the party is laying out how it plans to wield power, while President Trump and Republicans react to their midterm losses.

item.title: Judge blocks construction on Trump's 250-foot arch for now
item.description: The National Capital Planning Commission voted Thursday to approve plans for President Trump's 250-foot triumphal arch. A judge quickly blocked any construction from starting.

item.title: Trump signs proclamation declaring Oval Office a national monument
item.description: The action does not prevent future presidents from restyling the iconic office that President Trump has filled to the brim with gold flourishes, nor does it prevent a successor from rolling back the proclamation itself.

item.title: FEMA backlog causes delays in California infrastructure projects
item.description: FEMA is behind on approving major projects to protect Southern California from floods, earthquakes, fires and landslides.

item.title: Watch: Dangerous flooding hits Georgia, Tennessee
item.description: Torrential rain hammered Georgia and Tennessee overnight, triggering catastrophic flooding in certain areas. Videos show the floods, damage and rescue efforts.

item.title: Nithya Raman ousts incumbent Karen Bass in LA mayor's race, CBS News projects
item.description: Raman's win comes after resounding victories for Democrats across the country on Election Day.

item.title: Wendy's rejects $1.4 billion hostile takeover bid
item.description: Wendy's rebuffs unsolicited offer from Trian Partners, led by activist investor Nelson Peltz, and another group of investment firms.

item.title: Democrats have flipped over 40 House seats. Here's the breakdown.
item.description: Democrats won control of the House on Tuesday by flipping more than three dozen Republican-held seats, picking up perennial swing districts and seats that were once considered deep red.

item.title: New details, bodycam video of deadly Citibank shooting
item.description: A gunman targeted Citibank employees on Wednesday, holding them responsible for a $2,500 credit card bill, a Florida sheriff said. Cristian Benavides reports on the new details and bodycam video from the scene.

item.title: Georgia competition honors exemplary young trade workers
item.description: The Georgia Skills Challenge, an annual series of competitions, brings together the state's best young tradespeople. There is glory at stake, but also money from real jobs. Tony Dokoupil has more.

item.title: Newsom moves to commute all California death sentences
item.description: The move does not repeal California's death penalty or prevent prosecutors from seeking it in future cases.

item.title: Indiana, Florida and Alabama carry out 3 U.S. executions on the same day
item.description: This marks the second time this year that three people in the U.S. were put to death on a single day.

item.title: Mississippi Senate race is toss-up, with razor-thin margin
item.description: The Senate race in deep-red Mississippi remains unresolved, as Democrat Scott Colom has mounted a surprisingly competitive challenge to incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

item.title: Pete Hegseth doubles down on Iran war in new video despite election losses
item.description: In a new video posted to X, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth vowed to keep fighting Iran, despite many blaming Republicans' midterm losses on the war. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: The new voice of Boston Logan Airport on winning contest: "I am so honored"
item.description: Massport, the agency that runs Boston Logan Airport, says that more than 6,000 people auditioned to be the new voice of the airport. HVAC pipefitter Chris Donisi of Burlington, Massachusetts, took home the highest honor of becoming the new voice of the airport. He joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Political twists and turns of the 2026 midterms
item.description: CBS News' Michael George breaks down the top political headlines from the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: Voters pass 44 ballot measures to restrict data centers on Election Day
item.description: Voters passed 44 measures to restrict data centers on Election Day amid concerns over their power usage and potential job losses tied to artificial intelligence. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Trump lawyers try to appeal convictions in his Stormy Daniels "hush money" case
item.description: Judges grilled President Trump's lawyers on Thursday as they try to get his conviction in the Stormy Daniels "hush money" case thrown out. The president was convicted of 34 felonies by a unanimous jury tied to a 2016 payment to adult film star Stormy Daniels. Now, his team argues that some of the evidence presented to jurors may be subject to presidential immunity. CBS News legal analyst Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: 2 women go farthest in Navy SEAL training than ever before
item.description: Two women went farther than any other female candidates in the Navy SEALs' demanding tryouts, even though they didn't pass the course. Women have only been eligible to attempt the notoriously difficult training since 2015. CBS News Pentagon reporter Eleanor Watson reports.

item.title: What's next as Mississippi, Alaska Senate races still too close to call
item.description: Initial vote counts in Mississippi and Alaska's Senate races show the Democratic candidates with razor-thin leads over the Republicans. CBS News' Fin Gómez discusses what's next.

item.title: Catastrophic flooding in Georgia, Tennessee
item.description: Georgia's governor declared a state of emergency in at least four counties on Thursday due to dangerous flooding. Tennessee was also hit hard, with dozens of people rescued from homes and roads. Skyler Henry reports and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: French workers flood streets for anti-government protests
item.description: Thousands of government workers, teachers, transport employees and other union workers in France walked off the job Thursday to express their frustration with low wages and the high cost of living.

item.title: Dolly Parton's estate moves to dismiss lawsuit against nephew
item.description: The details of the resolution between Dolly Parton's estate and her nephew, Bryan Seaver, were not immediately known.

item.title: Stocks crater as midterms spur investor exodus from tech and AI
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq is now in a "correction" as Wall Street weighs the impact of the Democrats' wins on the critical AI sector.

item.title: English teacher on how she uses AI to help students learn
item.description: Many schools are pushing artificial intelligence out of the classroom, worried that students will use AI instead of thinking for themselves. But some educators are embracing the technology and say it is helping students learn. Meg Oliver reports from DREAM East Harlem Middle School in New York City.

item.title: Trump agenda likely to be curbed with Democrats in charge
item.description: Investigations, a struggle to confirm nominees and maybe some bipartisanship lie ahead for President Trump.

item.title: Did GOP efforts to redistrict the House turn into a dummymander?
item.description: Republicans undertook a historic effort to redraw several states' Congressional districts mid-decade in an attempt to maintain control of the House.

item.title: 11/5: CBS Evening News
item.description: Police say a gunman targeted bank employees over credit card debt; catastrophic flooding triggers evacuations and rescue efforts.

item.title: Trump's lawyers argue appeal in "hush money" case
item.description: President Trump was convicted in 2024 of 34 felonies tied to a 2016 "hush money" payment to adult film star Stormy Daniels.

item.title: Hoax bomb threats affect at least 20 European flights within hours
item.description: At least 20 flights in Europe deal with bomb threats, adding to what one expert calls an unusual level of hoaxes in a short time period, suggesting "a very deliberate act."
